Kept as a separate record per the duplicate-file rule; merge into 1183 or drop at Mahesh's discretion. See 1183.json for the full research. Summary repeated here: Hindu Kali temple on the outskirts of Malda town (Laha Bari/Jhaljhalia/Rina Road area; listings also give Raipur and New Banshbari - location naming inconsistent). Local tradition gives two conflicting origins: the original temple built in 1500 AD, or built by Raja Ballal Sen (1159-1179), third Sena-dynasty ruler. The deity's three faces are said to represent Maha Kali, Maha Lakshmi and Maha Saraswati (unverified). Puja traditionally on Saturdays and Tuesdays; an annual mela in Baisakh amid the region's GI-tagged Fazli mango gardens.

name: Maa Jahura Temple (Jauhra Kali)
town_description: Malda (English Bazar) is a city in northern West Bengal on the Mahananda river, famous for its GI-tagged Fazli, Langra and Himsagar mangoes. The district preserves the medieval capitals of Gaur (Gauda) and Pandua, whose Sultanate-era mosques and tombs draw heritage travellers.

travel.airport: Bagdogra International Airport (IXB), roughly 230 km north, is the nearest major airport.
travel.railway: Malda Town Junction (MLDT), a major station, is a few km away.
travel.road: On the outskirts of Malda town near Laha Bari/Jhaljhalia (Rina Road area); reachable by local auto-rickshaw or taxi from Malda town.

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; the annual Baisakh mela (April-May) draws the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Conflicting reports: one listing says 6 AM-3 PM daily; another says open only Tuesdays and Saturdays (7 AM-1 PM and 5 PM-8 PM); a review says puja is offered only on Saturdays and Tuesdays (verify).
